current_state_facts.phase4_c35_note: 0026 corrects a measured defect: the 0025 gate passed as soon as ANY compliance archive row existed, so the local export written by the same appliance that was about to delete the data authorized the deletion -- self-certification. The gate now requires receipt_verified, and ca_receipt_evidence_matches_flag makes that flag unsettable without a named external authority, a reference and a timestamp -- refused even for the table owner, refused on INSERT, and p4_record_compliance_receipt is granted to NO role. No external archival receipt authority exists in this product, so receipt_verified is false everywhere and CROSS-CUSTOMER PURGE IS CONSEQUENTLY IMPOSSIBLE. That is the delivered behaviour and it is intended: a capability that cannot be performed safely is unavailable rather than available on weaker evidence. scd's purge path reports the exact blocker and the appliance stays fail-closed. The gate is not 'always refuse': recording a receipt with real external evidence opens it, which is proved.

current_state_facts.governance_tooling_isolation: The adversarial mutation suite runs every mutation in a disposable sandbox built by `git clone --shared --no-checkout` plus a copy of the working tree and of .git/index, and it PROVES fidelity before mutating anything: `git status --porcelain` and `git ls-files -s` (blob ids, stage numbers, modes) must both match the checkout exactly. It fails closed if the sandbox cannot be built, digests the canonical governance/ before and after, and refuses to run at all under --require-full while the test-only MUTATION_MAX_CASES is set. Forced kills cannot run handlers, so sandbox cleanup after SIGKILL/TerminateProcess is NOT claimed; the canonical checkout is untouched regardless, and a startup sweep in the next run collects the leftover. Proved by tools/tests/project_state_validator/run_isolation_regression.py, 13/13.

phase3_delivery_evidence.protocol: The numeric Software/Governance run ids, the artifact id and the artifact integrity SHA-256 are DELIBERATELY not recorded in any committed document. They describe the CI run that the delivery commit itself triggers, so a committed artifact could only ever cite a previous round's values -- which is the exact staleness the Zero-Stale rule exists to prevent. They live in the PR #6 body, which is written after the run completes and is independently verified. The Zero-Stale validator enforces this protocol by failing if any numeric run or artifact id appears in the Final Report.
